expected_fault: VLAN 20 was never created in the switch VLAN database. Fa0/3 is assigned to an inactive VLAN, so frames are dropped even though the port is up.
Fa0/5 is assigned to VLAN 30 (Guest) instead of VLAN 20 (Sales), so the host leases from the Guest DHCP scope.
VLAN 40 is missing from the trunk's allowed VLAN list on Gi0/1, so its frames are pruned at the inter-switch link.
Native VLAN mismatch across the trunk: SW1 uses VLAN 1, SW2 uses VLAN 99. Untagged traffic leaks between VLANs and STP behaves inconsistently.
The inter-switch link was left in static access mode in VLAN 1 instead of being configured as an 802.1q trunk, so only VLAN 1 crosses it.
PC2's default gateway is set to 192.168.10.254, which does not exist. The real gateway is 192.168.10.1.
The configured default gateway 192.168.11.1 is outside PC3's own 192.168.10.0/24 subnet, so the host has no route to reach it.
No 'ip default-gateway' is configured on the Layer 2 switch, so it can reach its local subnet but cannot originate traffic off-net.
The router-on-a-stick configuration is missing the Gi0/0.30 subinterface for VLAN 30, so that VLAN has no Layer 3 gateway.
The DHCP pool is fully exhausted (244 of 244 leased), so late clients fall back to APIPA addressing.
The DHCP pool network statement is 192.168.99.0/24 but the serving interface is in 192.168.10.0/24, so clients get addresses from the wrong subnet.
The DHCP pool hands out default-router 192.168.10.254, which is not a real gateway. The router's LAN address is 192.168.10.1.
Gi0/0.20 has no 'ip helper-address', so VLAN 20 DHCP broadcasts are never relayed to the server at 192.168.10.5.
The host points at 192.168.10.53 as its DNS server, but the actual DNS service runs on 192.168.10.5. No device answers at .53.
The DNS service is toggled Off on the server. The host and its records are fine, the daemon simply is not answering.
The A record for www.lab.local points to 192.168.20.99, which is not assigned to any host. The web server is 192.168.20.10.
R1 has no route to 192.168.30.0/24 and no default route, so it drops the traffic and returns an ICMP unreachable.
The static route points to next-hop 10.0.0.9, which does not exist. The actual neighbour on the /30 link is 10.0.0.2.
No default route (0.0.0.0/0) toward the ISP is configured on R1, so packets for outside destinations have no matching route.
The shared link is in OSPF area 0 on R1 but area 1 on R2. Area IDs must match on a common segment for adjacency to form.
The static route was written with mask 255.255.255.192 (/26) instead of /24, so only the first 62 hosts of the LAN are covered.
ACL 101 is applied outbound on Gi0/0, so it filters traffic heading toward the LAN rather than traffic sourced from it. It should be applied inbound.
ACL entry ordering is wrong. The broad deny at sequence 10 matches first, so the specific permit at sequence 20 is never evaluated.
ACL 120 only permits TCP 80 and 443. The implicit 'deny ip any any' at the end drops UDP 53 (DNS) and UDP 67/68 (DHCP).
GUEST_FILTER is applied inbound on Gi0/0.10 (the internal VLAN) instead of Gi0/0.50 (the guest VLAN), so guest-sourced traffic is never evaluated. Zero matches confirm it.
Neither interface is marked with 'ip nat inside' or 'ip nat outside', so the NAT rule never engages. Note the empty interface lists in show ip nat statistics.
The NAT source ACL only permits 192.168.10.0/24. VLAN 20 traffic is not matched, so it leaves untranslated and is dropped upstream.
The 'overload' keyword is missing from the NAT statement, so the router does one-to-one NAT instead of PAT. With a single public IP only one host can translate at a time.
The guest SSID is mapped to internal VLAN 10 instead of guest VLAN 50. Guests land directly on the internal subnet, bypassing GUEST_FILTER entirely.
Security mode mismatch: the AP runs WPA2-PSK with AES while the client is set to WEP. The authentication method must match on both sides.
VLAN 60 has no Layer 3 gateway subinterface and no DHCP pool. Association succeeds at Layer 2, but there is nothing to serve addresses, so clients fall back to APIPA.
R1 Gi0/1 was left in a shutdown state. 'administratively down' means the interface was never brought up with 'no shutdown'.
Duplex mismatch on the uplink: SW1 Gi0/2 is full-duplex while SW2 Gi0/2 is half-duplex. The late collision and CRC counters confirm it.
